s24.question: Between November 2025 and February 2026, porosity went up across several people's trials even though nobody changed their recipes. What changed? Cite the evidence.
s24.answer:
What changed was the mixer, not the recipes. From November 2025 to January 2026, trials were mixed on "Planetary mixer #2 (loaner unit)" [T161-L04], [T163-L04], [T168-L04], [T170-L04], [T175-L04], [T181-L04], [T182-L04]. By March they were back on the main planetary mixer [T194-L04], [T195-L04], [T200-L04]. The notebook doesn't say why the loaner was used. On the loaner, the degassed trials stayed low: [T161] 0.79%, [T162] 0.54%, [T168] 0.44%, all passing, with Ines's vacuum degas logged each time [T161-L06], [T162-L06], [T168-L06]. The trials that skipped degassing failed: [T170] 6.56%, [T181] 6.97%, [T182] 2.84%, [T163] 1.55%, and [T175] 1.01%. Skipping degas on the main mixer did not always fail: [T147] at 0.6% and [T200] at 0.31% passed, while [T160] (1.35%, October) and [T195] (1.25%, March) failed.

Hypothesis: the loaner may whip more air into the thinner resin, and without vacuum degassing those bubbles stay in the cured part. Brittle resin is flaw-sensitive, so bubbles may act as cracks. Ines's habit of degassing every trial may be why her winter trials held.

Uncertain: only five no-degas trials ran on the loaner, and the notebook has no mixer calibration or ambient records, so I can't separate the mixer from operator or room effects. Ledger item [L10] is still open and cites [T161], [T162] and [T163].
